quote: Theorem: Suppose X1 ~ TL − TIIEHL − MO − G(b1, α, δ, ξ) and X2 ~ TL − TIIEHL − MO − G(b2, α, δ, ξ). If b1 < b2, then f(x;b1,α,δ,ξ)/f(x;b2,α,δ,ξ) is decreasing in x. ... If b1 < b2, then ∂/∂x [f(x;b1,α,δ,ξ)/f(x;b2,α,δ,ξ)] < 0, which implies that likelihood ratio order exist among X1 and X2, that is, X2 <lr X1.
family: Topp-Leone type II exponentiated half logistic–Marshall-Olkin-G family TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b, α, δ, ξ) over baseline G(·;ξ)
compared: Topp-Leone parameters b1 < b2; common α, δ, ξ

hypotheses.text: X1 ~ TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b1, α, δ, ξ), X2 ~ TL-TIIEHL-MO-G(b2, α, δ, ξ); b1 < b2

conclusion.direction: X2 <=_lr X1 as printed (the ratio f1/f2 decreasing would instead mean X1 <=_lr X2 — see ambiguity)

ambiguity: The printed conclusion 'X2 <lr X1' is inconsistent with f1/f2 decreasing, which under the stated definition (f_X/f_Y decreasing ⟹ X <lr Y) gives X1 <lr X2; direction likely transposed in print.

quote: As a result, we conclude that X1 and X2 are stochastically ordered, that is, X1 <st X2.
compared: b1 < b2; common α, δ, ξ

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_st X2 (as printed; opposite to the printed lr direction)
